findings.text: the report lists "promoted" among the facts it attributes to plan comment c-awcj-proving-run at plan:859-860, but that comment records only the run's execution (compute node 98dci4-clu-3036, job 1274056, partition all, 4 cores / 16 GiB granted, 129 s, zero queue wait) and says nothing about a promotion; the plan's only promotion record for that run is the failure its followup captures (plan:805, "reckon crew complete on the placed run raises no launch translation for command 'srun'"), nothing else in the plan records a retry, the ledger carries no row for the run (docs/state/reckon/crew.json at base: 0 of 1912 rows match placed-proof or 1274056, against 8 rows for the plan's other awcj nodes), and no commit names it — so section 1's done-when clause "is promoted without any special handling" (plan:119) is recorded landed on a source that does not carry it.

the report says the follower's stall event carries "stalled_for_seconds and no liveness field in the event"; the event at reckon/crew/recovery.py:5666-5671 is a spread of the classified row with stalled_for_seconds added, and that row comes from classify_pointer (recovery.py:5634-5636), which carries process_alive (recovery.py:4254) and liveness_proven (recovery.py:4259), so a liveness field is present in the event and the reproduction claim is overstated — the ticker half of the same paragraph is sound, since the report itself notes the row already carries process_alive at recovery.py:4705 and only the word drops it.

item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed manifest reads status complete, records no repository commit in a prose commits line carrying the base sha, and records no test run with the read-only fence as the reason, which matches the fence the report itself names in its method line.
